name: Moksha

ancestors.notes: Mordvinic branch of Uralic; Republic of Mordovia, Russia.

notes: Moksha (мокшень кяль), Mordvinic (Uralic), Russia. Written in a Cyrillic alphabet identical in inventory to Russian. Palatalisation is phonemic and is written the Russian way, with the soft sign <ь> or an iotated vowel letter <е ё ю я> after the consonant. So <е ё ю я> read ʲV after a consonant letter and jV elsewhere: at the start of a word (<ялга> [jalɡa]), after a vowel (<лия> [lʲijæ]) and after <ь> (<кундья> [kunʲdʲja]). Hamari and Ajanki (hamari_ajanki2022, p. 394, note b to Table 23.3, which the Moksha Table 23.4 refers to) state the jV value: "When /j/ is followed by a vowel both the consonant and the vowel are indicated with a single grapheme in the orthography—the one that also indicates the palatalization of an alveolar: je ‹е›, ju ‹ю›, jɑ ‹я›, jo ‹ё›". The alphabet description (mordvinic_alphabets_wiki) gives each of the four letters both values: "sound [a] after palatal consonants, as well as combination with the preceding й", and "Palatalization is indicated by the letter ь after the consonant or by the letters е, ё, и, ю, я after the consonant." Moksha additionally has voiceless sonorants, spelled <лх>, <рх>, <йх>. The reduced vowel /ə/ is not given its own letter — it is spelled <о>/<е>/<а> depending on context — so it appears here only as an allophone. Stress is largely on the first syllable but is not written.

sources.notes: p. 394, note b to Table 23.3 (Table 23.4, Moksha, refers to it): "When /j/ is followed by a vowel both the consonant and the vowel are indicated with a single grapheme in the orthography—the one that also indicates the palatalization of an alveolar: je ‹е›, ju ‹ю›, jɑ ‹я›, jo ‹ё›". Note a: "Palatalization is indicated in the orthography with either the following vowel (see Table 23.1) or—in the absence of a vowel—with the soft sign ь." Moksha examples: пеель pejǝlj, юр jur (p. 398). Open accepted manuscript: https://www.utupub.fi/handle/10024/191945.

sources.notes: Modern Mordvin alphabet: е ё ю я are the vowel "after palatal consonants, as well as combination with the preceding й" (Я я: "sound [a] after palatal consonants, as well as combination with the preceding й"), and "Palatalization is indicated by the letter ь after the consonant or by the letters е, ё, и, ю, я after the consonant." The Russian article it translates (Мордовская письменность) says the same: "Я я — звук [a] после мягких согласных, а также сочетание с предшествующим й."
